messages:
jen-support: FYI — ACME escalated: streaming request got marked as 5xx when their client sent a FIN in the middle of a chunk. They say this caused billing disputes. attaching trace id and sample payload. :frowning:

sam-ops: Can you drop the trace_id and a request sample? Also which SDK / agent?

jen-support: trace_id=tr_20260317_7a9c3b. SDK: client-js v2.8.1. They sent a multipart chunked stream; payload snip below.

jen-support: ```
POST /v1/generate/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: application/json

7
{"prompt":"start"}
3e
{"tokens": [ ... ]   <-- client mid-chunk, then socket FIN
```

sam-ops: thanks. Do we have gateway logs correlated to that trace_id? 

maria-sre: looking. I see the gateway recorded a socket half-close while upstream runtime was still producing. Our current heuristic classifies a mid-response client FIN as a 5xx if runtime had pending output and no trailer. That might be the billing culprit.

alex-rt: hmm. Is this the same path as the chunked EOF heuristic change from March rollout? deploy-bot: rollout v1.3.2 applied 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC

maria-sre: yes, heuristic tightened -- we now conservatively mark requests as server-failure when a FIN arrives mid-chunk and the runtime hasn't sent a final chunk/trailer. It was to avoid silent truncation billing. But it mislabels client-initiated aborts in some proxy setups.

jen-support: ACME claims they closed because mobile network flapped; they expect client-close not to be billed. They provided a packet capture showing FIN from client before server finished.

sam-ops: action items: get a minimal repro, see if our FIN detection is mis-ordered with proxy halfclose, and check billing classification path. I'll try to reproduce with a curl + raw TCP client.

alex-rt: repro suggestion: run a simple node stream that writes a partial chunk then issues socket.end() mid-chunk. Example (pseudo):

```
const net = require('net');
const s = net.connect({host: 'api.redwood.ai', port: 443});
s.write('...chunk headers...');
setTimeout(()=> s.end(), 50); // FIN mid-chunk
```

maria-sre: also share gateway logs for socket-state transitions: we need timestamps for recv(FIN), upstream write status, and any trailer emission. If the gateway sees FIN before runtime flush, current code sets 5xx.

jen-support: ACME gave sample timestamps: client FIN at 2026-03-17T15:04:12.987Z, gateway recv FIN 15:04:13.012Z, runtime final token at 15:04:13.045Z (they captured the server bytes). So gateway saw FIN ~33ms before runtime final bytes.

alex-rt: that 33ms window is nasty. If runtime finishes after FIN but before OS-level close, we might be able to retroactively classify as client-close if final bytes were sent. Need to check if gateway buffers/queues affect ordering.

sam-ops: quick log excerpt for tr_20260317_7a9c3b (gateway):
```
[15:04:12.988] conn=5678 read=512 bytes
[15:04:13.012] conn=5678 recv FIN
[15:04:13.015] dispatched to runtime r=34
[15:04:13.040] runtime wrote chunk id=89
[15:04:13.046] gateway classified event=client_abort -> 5xx (billing=true)
```

maria-sre: that shows we classified before runtime wrote final chunk. The final chunk made it out of runtime at 13.040 but gateway classified at 13.046 — ordering suggests we marked 5xx after runtime write but before we observed the bytes on the wire. We need to inspect the codepath that decides classification (is it based on observed recv events vs observed egress?).

alex-rt: probable race between our connection state machine and egress ack handler. Fix options: 1) wait a small grace window (50-100ms) before final classification for halfclose cases, 2) correlate runtime event ids (if runtime signals completion, treat as success even if FIN seen), 3) consult trailer frames. Each has tradeoffs w.r.t. latency and billing accuracy.

jen-support: customer asks for a timeline & mitigation ASAP. Suggested interim: exempt ACME from billing for any requests with trace_id prefix tr_20260317_*. Can we do that?

sam-ops: we can apply a billing override for that trace range. I'll put in a temporary rule and notify billing. 

maria-sre: longer term, I'll spike a fix to defer 5xx classification when FIN observed within X ms and runtime signals eventual completion. I'll open a PR and add unit + e2e for the halfclose path.

alex-rt: I'll reproduce locally and attach a small python repro to the ticket so support can use it for customer validation.

jen-support: great. ACME wants an ETA for rollback/fix. Can we commit a mitigation in 24h? 

sam-ops: billing override done (case# BIL-2207), pinged billing ops. Mitigation PR planned, ETA 48h for canary, 72h for full rollout given test matrix.

jen-support: thanks team. I'll update ACME with the override and timelines. :thumbsup:
